properties.description: Add your JavaScript custom logic here.
properties.label: JavaScript Code
properties.name: script

properties.description: Chooses where and how this task's code runs. Each runner type shows its own settings, and only the runners an operator has enabled are offered.
properties.label: Task Runner
properties.name: taskRunner

properties.description: Where this task runs. GraalVM runs JavaScript or Python inside the server and is the only runner that gives the code a context, with component and log. Process starts the interpreter as a program on the server's machine. Docker, Kubernetes and AWS Batch run the code in a container. Bash scripts and commands need Process or a container runner.
properties.label: Type
properties.name: type

properties.description: The container image the code runs in, as a registry reference such as ghcr.io/acme/tools:1.4. It must contain the interpreter for the action's language. Defaults to an official image for the language: Ubuntu for Bash and shell commands, Node.js for JavaScript and Python for Python.
properties.label: Image
properties.name: image

properties.description: Replaces the interpreter as a list of arguments, such as python3 and -u. The script or commands file is appended as the last argument either way. Defaults to the interpreter for the action's language.
properties.label: Entrypoint
properties.name: entrypoint

properties.description: The user the code runs as inside the container, as a name or a numeric uid[:gid], such as 1000:1000. Defaults to the image's own user, often root.
properties.label: User
properties.name: user

properties.description: How many CPUs the container may use, such as 0.5 or 2. Empty means no limit.
properties.label: CPU
properties.name: cpu

properties.description: The most memory the container may use, in bytes or with a b, k, m or g suffix, such as 512m or 2g. The container is stopped when it uses more. Empty means no limit.
properties.label: Memory
properties.name: memory

properties.description: The network the container joins: bridge (Docker's default, with internet access), none (no network at all), host (the Docker host's own network), or the name of a user-defined network, to reach other containers on it.
properties.label: Network Mode
properties.name: networkMode

properties.description: Extra entries for the container's hosts file, each written as host:ip, such as api.internal:10.0.0.5. Use host.docker.internal:host-gateway to reach the Docker host.
properties.label: Extra Hosts
properties.name: extraHosts

properties.description: Runs the container with every capability of the Docker host and access to its devices. Off by default; turn it on only for trusted code that needs it, such as Docker in Docker.
properties.label: Privileged
properties.name: privileged

properties.description: Credentials for pulling the image from a private registry: a username and password, or a registry token instead.
properties.label: Registry Credentials
properties.name: credentials

properties.description: The registry's address, such as ghcr.io or registry.example.com:5000.
properties.label: Registry
properties.name: registry

properties.description: The user name for the registry.
properties.label: Username
properties.name: username

properties.description: The password or access token of the registry user.
properties.label: Password
properties.name: password

properties.description: A token for the registry, used instead of a username and password.
properties.label: Registry Token
properties.name: registryToken

properties.description: How long the container may take to stop on its own when the task is killed, on a timeout or a shutdown it cannot resume from, before it is forced, as an ISO-8601 duration such as PT30S. The default PT0S forces it at once.
properties.label: Kill Grace Period
properties.name: killGracePeriod

properties.description: When the image is pulled from its registry. Always pulls it on every run, so a moving tag such as latest stays current. If Not Present, the default, pulls it only when it is not there yet. Never uses only an image that is already there and fails without one.
properties.label: Pull Policy
properties.name: pullPolicy

properties.description: After a server restart, re-attach to the job this task execution already started and wait for its result instead of starting the code again. On by default; when off, a restart starts a new job.
properties.label: Resume
properties.name: resume

properties.description: Removes the job and whatever it left behind once it has finished. On by default; turn it off to inspect a failed job by hand.
properties.label: Delete
properties.name: delete

properties.description: How long the job may take to be scheduled, pull its image and start, as an ISO-8601 duration such as PT10M, the default. Raise it for large images or busy clusters.
properties.label: Wait Until Running
properties.name: waitUntilRunning

properties.description: How long the job may run once started before it is killed, as an ISO-8601 duration such as PT1H, the default. The task's Timeout, when set, takes precedence; both are capped by the operator's max-wait.
properties.label: Wait Until Completion
properties.name: waitUntilCompletion

properties.description: Strict runs the script with no access to the host: no file system, no environment, no process creation, and CPU and memory ceilings.
properties.label: Mode
properties.name: mode

properties.description: The program the script or commands file is handed to, such as bash or /usr/local/bin/python3. It must be installed on the server's machine. Defaults to bash for Bash, node for JavaScript, python3 for Python and /bin/sh for shell commands, looked up on the server's PATH.
properties.label: Interpreter
properties.name: interpreter

properties.description: Passes the server process's own environment variables to the code as well as the Environment property. Off by default, because that environment holds the server's credentials, such as database passwords and API keys. Turn it on only for code you trust with them.
properties.label: Inherit Environment
properties.name: inheritEnvironment

properties.description: Environment variables the script or commands see, as name and value pairs. The host's own environment is not passed on unless the Process runner's Inherit Environment option is on, so add every variable the code needs here. ByteChef also sets BYTECHEF_WORKING_DIR (the folder the code runs in), BYTECHEF_OUTPUT_DIR, BYTECHEF_INPUT_FILE and, when the task has connections, BYTECHEF_CONNECTIONS_FILE.
properties.label: Environment
properties.name: env

properties.description: Files placed in the working folder (BYTECHEF_WORKING_DIR) before the code runs, keyed by file name. A name may include folders, such as data/orders.csv. A value is either inline text, written as is, or a file from an earlier step, such as another task's output file, whose content is copied in. The code reads them by name, relative to the working folder.
properties.label: Input Files
properties.name: inputFiles

properties.description: Glob patterns for the files to keep from the output folder (BYTECHEF_OUTPUT_DIR) after the code finishes, such as *.csv or charts/summary.png. Each matching file is stored and returned in the task's outputFiles, keyed by its path relative to the output folder, so a later step can use it, for example task_1.outputFiles['report.csv']. Without patterns no file is kept and outputFiles is empty. Files that match no pattern are discarded, and output.json is never kept as a file because it becomes the task's vars.
properties.label: Output Files
properties.name: outputFiles

properties.description: How many seconds the code may run before it is stopped and the task fails. When empty, Process and GraalVM's Trusted mode stop it after 5 minutes, and container runners use Wait Until Completion. For container runners the operator's max-wait caps it.
properties.label: Timeout (seconds)
properties.name: timeout
